action_summary: Runs the previous round's pre-registered falsifier and answers it: a record-based commit DOES recover byte-exactly from a crash between two single-path renames, so multi-path commits have a sound portable implementation and last round's residual -- atomic only where the filesystem can exchange two populated paths -- is dissolved rather than engineered around. A 6-operation real commit (GNU tar extracting five members, rm deleting one) is crashed at all 10 boundaries: before the record the tree is provably still the pre-state and there is no record (all-or-nothing); at and after the durable record all 8 boundaries recover to the target byte-exactly; a crash after cleanup finds the target with nothing to replay. Recovery is itself crashed inside every one of its steps: 56 of 56 second recoveries reach the target. The no-record control leaves a tree that is neither state at 5 of 9 boundaries with nothing to recover from -- which is exactly why the previous round's single-rename limit was real. 868-byte record, 16 fsyncs, 7 renames per 6-operation commit. The durable record, not the sequence of renames, is the commit.

causal_blocker: The commit is now portable: a durable per-path record makes a multi-path commit recoverable byte-exactly without RENAME_EXCHANGE, so an arbitrary effect over a local tree is reversible on NFS, CIFS, Windows and anywhere plain rename exists. What remains is not atomicity but scope: the record can only describe effects that live in the tree, and fsync is a promise the device can break.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: Speculative forecast only. The round removes the last filesystem-capability dependency from committing an arbitrary effect; no truth obligation is discharged.

measured_effect.commit_point: the durable record, not the first rename

next_step: Test the durability the record now relies on, at the layer where it can actually be tested: drive the same commit under dm-log-writes and replay the block log at every crash point, to see whether the record and the tree survive a power cut (not a process kill) in the same order. Prediction: the tree never contains a half-written file, and the record is either absent (pre-state) or complete (replayable), because every step is fsync(file) -> rename -> fsync(dir). Falsifier: if any replayed image contains a torn or zero-length file, or a record that names operations whose pre-images were never durable, then the ordering is wrong and the record cannot be trusted after power loss -- which would put the residual back in the mechanism instead of the device.
real_outcome: That multi-path commit atomicity is a solved, portable problem with no new syscall: the durable record is the commit, operations are idempotent per path by digest, replay is a fold over those digests, and the whole thing is crash-safe against a crash inside recovery itself (56/56). The residual named last round is gone; what replaces it is the scope of an effect (a tree, not a network) and the honesty of the device's flush.

truth.the_law_this_round_adds: A commit is atomic exactly where its record is durable: write the record, fsync it, then any number of idempotent single-path steps, and a crash anywhere after the record replays to the target -- measured at 8/8 boundaries and 56/56 crashes inside recovery, with a pre-record crash provably leaving the pre-state. Atomicity stops being a filesystem capability and becomes a per-path digest condition.
what_is_false_in_the_claim: that a check mode is needed to decide an action: the five actions no check mode could guard are decided at 1.0 by attempting in a stage
that this tree's atomic publication is atomic: os.replace on a populated directory fails ENOTEMPTY, so it is atomic only for an absent target
that a refused attempt costs the world: 80 of 80 refusals left the live tree byte-identical
that one trial gives permanent knowledge of the effect: the effect is a function of the environment, and what is permanent is the licence to try
that trial-and-error is safe in general: only for effects confined to the staged tree; a network call, a process or an absolute path outside is not undoable here
that exchange is a compare-and-swap: confirmed against the Nov-2026 record, and the concurrency boundary is declared instead
that a multi-path commit needs RENAME_EXCHANGE, or a bigger syscall, to be atomic
that the commit point is the sequence of renames rather than the durable record
what_remains_open: power-loss durability: os._exit is not a power cut, and only dm-log-writes can test the order after one
the device may accept a flush and lie (PostgreSQL 2018), which no software can detect
scope: the record describes a tree, not a request already delivered to another machine
single-writer: two recoveries racing on one record are outside the contract
